blocks.caption: Figure 38.2-1 shows PCNT's architecture. As stated above, ctrl_ch0_u*n* is the control signal for ch0 of unit *n*. Its high and low states can be assigned different counter modes and used for pulse counting of the channel's input pulse signal sig_ch0_u*n* on negative or positive edges. The available counter modes are as follows:

c.v: Increment mode: When a channel detects an active edge of sig_ch0_u
(can be configured by software), the counter value pulse_cnt increases by 1.
If the channel's counter mode is changed or if PCNT_CNT_PAUSE_U
is set before pulse_cnt reaches PCNT_CNT_H_LIM_U
, then pulse_cnt freezes and its counter mode changes.
Decrement mode: When a channel detects an active edge of sig_ch0_u
(can be configured by software), the counter value pulse_cnt decreases by 1.
If the channel's counter mode is changed or if PCNT_CNT_PAUSE_U
is set before pulse_cnt reaches PCNT_CNT_H_LIM_U
, then pulse_cnt freezes and its counter mode changes.
Disable mode: Counting is disabled, and the counter value pulse_cnt freezes.
Table 38.2-1 to Table 38.2-4 provide information on how to configure the counter mode for channel 0.

c.v: Each unit has one filter for all its control and input pulse signals.
A filter can be enabled with the bit PCNT_FILTER_EN_U
The filter monitors the signals and ignores all the noise, i.e., the glitches with pulse widths shorter than PCNT_FILTER_THRES_U

Maximum count value: When pulse_cnt reaches PCNT_CNT_H_LIM_U

Minimum count value: When pulse_cnt reaches PCNT_CNT_L_LIM_U
